info.title: Home display server
info.description: What displays and monitors ask of the server that serves the dashboard image.

get.summary: A pass or fail for monitors: 200 unless the image is stale, then 503, with a line saying why.

200.description: The service is working. Includes `degraded` (a source is down and an earlier result stands in) and `failing` (renders are failing but the image is not yet stale).

500.description: The server could not work its state out.

503.description: The image is stale, or none has been rendered. The body says which.

text/plain.example: stale: the image is 3 h 0 min old

get.summary:
Serves the image in the format the client asked for with `Accept` (see `negotiate`): any it can
decode, the server's preferred one if it has no preference. 406 if it can decode none of them.
get.description:
The reply carries an `ETag` (a hash of the file), and a client that sends it back as `If-None-Match` is
answered 304 with no body when it already has that image.

A format whose file can't be inspected or read is skipped, so one bad file doesn't take the
others down with it. It is a 500 only when that leaves the client nothing it accepts, and never
a 404 or 406: those would say the image isn't there or isn't wanted, when the server failed.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description:
The display's name, so the server can tell displays apart (battery, last seen, which image it was sent).
A name that is not usable is ignored and the request is served all the same. Over HTTPS the display is
named by its certificate and this is ignored.

200.description: The image, in the best format the client accepts: BMP, PNG or QOI. The reply's `Content-Type` says which, and that is all a client needs to decode it.

cache-control.description: Always `no-store`: the picture changes every refresh.

content-length.description: The size of the file, which is how a dropped download is noticed.

etag.description: Identifies this file's bytes, so a client that keeps the picture can ask with `If-None-Match` whether it has changed.

vary.description: Always `Accept`, because the format depends on it.

304.description: The client's `If-None-Match` names the image it would be sent, so it already has it. No body.

etag.description: The same value the client sent.

406.description: The client accepts none of the formats there are. The body lists the ones available.

500.description: An image exists but could not be read, which is a failure of the server and not of the request.

get.summary: The same facts as `/status`, in the Prometheus text format, for a scraper.

200.description: The service's and the displays' state as Prometheus gauges (text exposition format 0.0.4), for a scraper. Everything in it is derived from the same data as `/status`, so the two agree.

text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8.example:
# HELP home_display_info The running version. Always 1.
# TYPE home_display_info gauge
home_display_info{version="0.1.0"} 1

500.description: The server could not work its state out.

get.summary: Tells a display which render the image is, whether it is stale, and when to ask again.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description:
The display's name, so the server can tell displays apart (battery, last seen, which image it was sent).
A name that is not usable is ignored and the request is served all the same. Over HTTPS the display is
named by its certificate and this is ignored.

parameters.name: have
parameters.description:
The version of the image the display already shows (the `version` of an earlier plan), so the answer can
say the image is unchanged and the display can skip the download and the refresh.

parameters.name: battery_mv
parameters.description: Battery voltage, in millivolts. Ignored unless a whole number from 2000 to 5000.

parameters.name: battery_pct
parameters.description: Battery charge, as a percentage. Ignored unless a whole number from 0 to 100.

parameters.name: battery_state
parameters.description: How the display rates its own battery. The display decides: the server only passes it on.

parameters.name: failed_wakes
parameters.description: How many wakes in a row have failed, for any reason.

parameters.name: rssi
parameters.description: Wi-Fi signal strength, in dBm. Ignored unless a whole number from -127 to -1.

parameters.name: last_failure
parameters.description: Why the wake before this one failed, if it did.

parameters.name: last_wake_s
parameters.description: How long the wake before this one was awake, in seconds: what costs battery. Ignored unless a whole number from 0 to 600.

parameters.name: last_tls_ms
parameters.description:
How long the display's first TLS handshake of the wake before this one took, in milliseconds, as the
display timed it (the server also times them, from its side: `connection` in `/status`).

parameters.name: last_heap_min
parameters.description:
The least free heap the display had during the wake before this one, in bytes: how close the handshake
came to running it out.

parameters.name: fw
parameters.description: The version of the firmware the display runs, as released (letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, at most 32).

200.description: The plan for the image there is.

schema.description: What a display is told after it asks: which image is current, whether it is out of date, and when to come back.

version.description: When the image was rendered, in seconds since 1970. Newer images have larger versions.

changed.description: False when the display said it already shows this version, so it can skip the download and refresh.

stale.description: A scheduled render is long overdue, so the image is older than it should be.

pending.description: A render is due or running, so a new image is about to appear.

next_seconds.description: How long the display should sleep before asking again.

age_seconds.description: Time since the image was rendered.

timezone.description:
The zone the server works in (an IANA name such as `Europe/London`), so the display needn't be told it in
its own configuration, where it could disagree.

utc_offset_seconds.description:
How far ahead of UTC that zone is right now, in seconds (3600 in the UK in summer). A display has no
timezone database, so this is what it needs to show local time; it is right until the next clock change.

404.description: Nothing has been rendered yet, so there is no image to plan around.

text/plain.example: No image has been rendered yet

500.description: The server could not work the plan out.

post.summary:
Renders now if the display's button asked for it (and one hasn't just run), then answers
like `/plan` for the image that results. A refused or failed render still answers, with the
image there is.

get.summary: How the service is doing: the render history, the sources' state, and the image's age.

200.description: The render history, the state of each data source, the displays that have checked in, and where each display stands in the certificate authority (empty over plain HTTP).

500.description: The server could not work its state out.

ConnectionStatus.description:
How a display's TLS connections have begun since the server started, from the server's side: it cannot be
misreported by the display, and the time includes the display's own work and the network between.

last_resumed.description: Whether the latest connection resumed a session (which saves the certificate exchange and signatures).

last_handshake_milliseconds.description: From accepting the latest connection to the end of its handshake.

DeliveryStatus.description: The last image a display was sent: which format, how big, and when.

DeviceStatus.description: A display that has checked in: its battery, signal and how its last wakes went.

name.description: The name the display gives itself.

expected_by.description: When the display was told to come back.

overdue.description: Later than it was told to be, plus the grace period.

wifi_rssi_dbm.description: Wi-Fi signal strength at the last check-in.

oneOf.description: Why the wake before that one failed, if it did.

last_wake_seconds.description: How long the wake before that one was awake, which is what costs battery.

last_tls_milliseconds.description: How long its first TLS handshake of the wake before took, as the display timed it.

last_heap_min_bytes.description: The least free heap it had during that wake, in bytes.

firmware.description: The version of the firmware it runs, as it said.

oneOf.description:
How its TLS connections have begun, as the server saw them: resumed or full, and how long the handshake
took. Empty for a display that has not connected over TLS since the server started.
The last image this display was sent, if it has fetched one since the server started.

FailureReason.description:
Why a display's last wake failed, as it reports it on the next wake that gets through. A wake can't
report its own failure (it asks `/plan` before it knows), and a Wi-Fi or server failure can only be
told once the display is talking to the server again.

ImageFormat.description: A file format the server can send an image in.

MemberStatus.description:
A display and where it stands in the certificate authority, for the owner to see trouble weeks before it
is one: a display that stopped renewing shows as a certificate running out.

certificate_not_after.description: For a member, when the latest certificate it was given ends.

certificate_expires_in_seconds.description: Seconds until then; negative once it has passed.

certificate_expired.description:
A member whose certificate has run out. Nothing to fix: it gets a new one by itself, with no one
at the server, the next time it is switched on.

renewal_overdue.description:
A member whose certificate should have been renewed by now and has not been (about 63 days after it was issued,
for a 90-day certificate): it has stopped renewing, though the certificate has not run out. Look at the display:
it may be off, out of range, or its clock or flash may be wrong. Once the certificate ends this is false and
`certificate_expired` says so instead.

changing_keys.description: It has been given a certificate for a new key and has not used it yet.

replacement_waiting.description: A different key is waiting for the owner to approve it taking this display's name.

SourceReport.description: One data source (weather, a departure board) and how it was on the last render.

oneOf.description: Failed, and shown from an earlier answer this many seconds old.
Failed, with nothing recent enough to show. `reason` is a few words, such as "key rejected".

SourceState.description: How a data source stood at the last render. `state` says which, and the fields beside it depend on it.

Status.description:
How the service is doing: the render history, the state of the data sources, the displays that have
checked in, and where each stands in the certificate authority.

sources.description: How each source was on the last successful render.

devices.description: The displays that have checked in, with their battery and whether any has gone quiet.

members.description: Where each display stands in the certificate authority. Empty over plain HTTP.

schedule.description: The refresh schedule in words, one line per cron expression.

tags.name: displays
tags.description: What a display asks of the server on each wake.

tags.name: monitoring
tags.description: How the service is doing, for monitors and for the owner.
